title: Red Shift by Alan Garner - Rerun
summary: A 2017 Backlisted episode, rebroadcast today, in which Erica Wagner and S.F. Said discuss Alan Garner's Red Shift, his fifth novel. They explore its layered, history-haunted storytelling and the strength of its narrative voice.

title: Archive: Frederick Douglass
summary: A 2018 In Our Time archive episode in which Melvyn Bragg and his guests discuss Frederick Douglass. The programme considers his Narrative of the Life, a powerful first-person account.

title: Lessons in Harmony by Jonathan Coe review – what can music tell us about national identity?
summary: The Guardian reviews Jonathan Coe's novel Lessons in Harmony, which imagines the friendship between Ravel and Ralph Vaughan Williams and their search for a musical identity. The review asks what music can tell us about national identity.

title: Daphnis and Chloe
summary: An appreciative Literary Hub essay on Longus's pastoral romance Daphnis and Chloe. The work opens with a prayer that it will bring pleasure and comfort to lovers, and the essay dwells on its lyrical, musical prose.

title: Review: Palme D'or winning film Fjord and Jonathan Coe's novel Lessons in Harmony
summary: BBC Radio 4's Front Row reviews Jonathan Coe's novel Lessons in Harmony, about the friendship between Ravel and Vaughan Williams. It also covers Tate Britain's Inside Bloomsbury exhibition on Vanessa Bell and Duncan Grant, and the Palme d'Or-winning film Fjord.

title: How Jan van Eyck transformed portraiture | National Gallery
summary: A National Gallery video on how Jan van Eyck made portraiture new in the fifteenth century. Curators from London and Bruges discuss his realism and the hidden visual clues in his work.

title: How the story of ‘the girl of 100 portraits’ inspired two books
summary: The story of Louise Cansot, the model behind 'the girl of 100 portraits', who was murdered in Paris in 1949 and forgotten by police. The piece links painting, a Goncourt-winning novel and a historical research project.

title: ‘His wife was horrified’: did Edward Hopper paint his sexual problems?
summary: A new Edward Hopper biography suggests that his marriage to Josephine Nivison Hopper, and their bedroom troubles, surfaced in famous works such as his melancholy paintings. The Guardian considers how far a painter's private life can be read into his canvases.

title: Paul Cézanne, pionnier de l'art moderne | ARTE
summary: A 2025 ARTE documentary by Grit Lederer, 53 minutes long, on Paul Cézanne. It follows his work back to Aix-en-Provence and the family bastide Jas de Bouffan, where he experimented before becoming a founder of modern art. Available on ARTE until 22 December 2026.

title: 1942 : un monde en guerre | Janvier - Mai | Documentaire | ARTE
summary: An ARTE documentary on 1942, the year the war became global, told through civilians around the world. Voices from Germany, Russia and Singapore give it a polyphonic structure. This is the January to May part of the series.

title: La Chimère sur Arte : Josh O'Connor pille les tombes étrusques pour retrouver un amour perdu
summary: Serie News introduces La Chimère, showing on ARTE. Josh O'Connor plays a man who plunders Etruscan tombs in search of a lost love. The piece presents it as a fiction with a strong romantic and archaeological premise.

title: Klaus Nomi : le destin tragique de l’ovni de la pop raconté dans un documentaire sur Arte
summary: TV-Programme.com highlights an ARTE documentary on Klaus Nomi, the avant-garde pop performer. The film tells his tragic story, and the article presents him as one of pop's true oddities.

title: The tomb in the mountain
summary: A World Service documentary on the Valley of Cuelgamuros, Franco's granite memorial basilica outside Madrid. It looks at the tens of thousands of war dead buried there.

title: Dr Miriam Stoppard
summary: Desert Island Discs with Dr Miriam Stoppard. Her life began in an Orthodox Jewish childhood in Newcastle, and moved through scholarship to a career in medicine.

title: I was kidnapped and held hostage for 977 days. Could I forgive my captors? – podcast
summary: Michael Scott Moore was held hostage for 977 days. He reflects on whether he could forgive his captors, and whether mercy might be mistaken for Stockholm syndrome. A podcast reading is available.

title: The horse made the state
summary: Lhamsuren Munkh-Erdene's Aeon essay argues that transport, especially the horse, rather than grain, enabled the rise of states. It follows conquest from the steppe to the sea.
